name: IEEE journals (general review criteria)

provenance.notes: IEEE has no single review form: each journal or society sets its own questionnaire in its submission system (ScholarOne/Manuscript Central). The criteria and the recommendation categories below are from the IEEE Author Center reviewer page (recommendations: Accept, Revise (Major or Minor), Reject; names vary by publication) and the IEEE Access best-practice page (technical, presentation and reference checks). Neither page gives numeric scales or the form layout. IEEE conferences use their own forms, which are not covered.

notes: IEEE Author Center: do not use AI tools (for example ChatGPT, Gemini) to generate or draft reviews. LLM-written content is therefore hidden in this export; only rule-based checks and quote-verified evidence are shown.

IEEE Access: do not share manuscript content with public AI platforms (treated as a confidentiality breach) and do not run submissions through plagiarism or AI-detection software. Turn the online checks off: they send the title, one abstract sentence and reference titles to Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv and OpenAlex.
Reviewers should check whether they can honour the confidentiality terms before accepting, and decline if a conflict of interest exists.

criteria: Contribution to the field and novelty.
Completeness of the literature review and appropriateness of the references.
Soundness of the methods and experimental design.
Quality and reproducibility of the results; benchmarking and validation sufficient.
Logical flow and strength of the conclusions; the conclusions follow from the data and analysis.
Organization, style and compliance with the publication requirements.
For revised articles: whether earlier comments were addressed, and the authors' response to reviewers.
Surveys, reviews and tutorials: coverage, new insights and long-term value.

sections.label: Summary of the work, merits and drawbacks
sections.guidance: Summarize the work and note its overall merits and drawbacks, with constructive, substantial feedback.

sections.label: Contribution and novelty
sections.guidance: Contribution to the field and novelty. Claims that work was done before need specific references.

sections.label: Literature review and references
sections.guidance: Is the background and motivation sufficient? Are references current and relevant? You may point out overlooked areas, but do not require specific articles (including your own) unless relevant, and explain why a suggested reference matters.

sections.label: Soundness of methods and experimental design
sections.guidance: Depth of the theoretical or experimental work, strength of the analysis, major technical flaws.

sections.label: Quality and reproducibility of results
sections.guidance: Quality of data and results, benchmarking and validation. If not reproducible, say what extra information is needed.

sections.label: Conclusions and logical flow
sections.guidance: Do the conclusions follow from the data and analysis? Does the information flow logically?

sections.label: Presentation
sections.guidance: Structure, language and writing style, quality of figures and tables, typos, formatting and compliance.

sections.label: Revised article: were earlier comments addressed?
sections.guidance: Only for revised submissions: check the authors' response to reviewers.

sections.label: Recommendation
sections.guidance: Decision names vary by publication: use your journal's options. Recommendations must be supported by specific, critical comments. Left for the human reviewer.
